title: One Month, Three Different Worlds
intro: You are going to read about the weather in January in three very different countries.

passage: What is the weather like in January? The answer depends on where you live. We asked three young people from different countries to tell us about their January. Their answers show how different the climate can be around the world.

Aiyna, 19, lives in Yakutsk, in the east of Russia. It is one of the coldest cities on Earth. "In January, the temperature is often minus 45 degrees," she says. "If you throw hot water into the air, it freezes before it hits the ground!" People wear two or three coats, and older children only stay at home from school when it is colder than about minus 50. "But I love our winter," Aiyna says. "The air is clean and the snow is beautiful."

For Jack, 22, from Sydney, Australia, January is one of the hottest months of the year. It is summer in the south of the world, and schools are closed for the long summer holiday. "We go to the beach almost every day," he says. "Sometimes it's 40 degrees, so we stay in the sea for hours." Even Christmas, in December, is hot. "We have Christmas dinner outside, in the sunshine." But summer is also a dangerous season. Every year, there are fires in the hot, dry forests.

In Mumbai, India, January is warm and pleasant, with blue skies. But Priya, 20, says her favourite time is June, when the monsoon begins. "It rains for hours every day, and the air is very humid," she explains. "There are often storms, and some streets flood. I always carry an umbrella, but I still get wet!" Farmers are happy, though, because their plants need the rain.

Here in Uzbekistan, January is usually cold, but not as cold as in Yakutsk. The snow often melts after a few days, and spring arrives in March. So before you visit a new country, check the weather forecast. In January, you may need a warm hat, or you may need sunglasses!
